Quench by adding saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate carefully, separate the organic layer, and extract the aqueous layer with dichloromethane or ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography, for example dichloromethane/methanol from 100:0 to 95:5, to afford the target pivalamide product.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or air, charge a dry reaction flask with BrCc1ccc(Br)nc1, 1.0 equiv, and acetonitrile, approximately 10 mL per mmol of bromomethyl bromopyridine. Add 1-ethylpiperazine, 1.2 equiv, followed by finely powdered potassium carbonate, 1.5 equiv. Stir the suspension at 50 °C for about 4 h, monitoring by LCMS or TLC for consumption of the bromomethyl starting material. After completion, cool to room temperature and filter through Celite to remove inorganic salts, washing the cake with acetonitrile or ethyl acetate. Concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure. full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with N-Boc-L-proline, 1-(isopropylsulfonyl)piperazine hydrochloride, and DMF. Add triethylamine at room temperature and stir for 5-10 min to liberate the free amine. Add HATU portionwise, maintaining the temperature near 25 °C. Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol, for example 0-10% methanol, optionally containing a small amount of ammonium hydroxide or triethylamine to reduce piperazine tailing, to afford the target Boc-proline piperazine amide.

patent_details: In a round-bottom flask with a nitrogen atmosphere and containing a mechanical stirrer, a thermometer and an addition funnel, was combined 1,073 grams (10.9 moles) of maleic anhydride (commercially available from Aldrich Chemical, Milwaukee, Wis.) and 6,062 grams of acetonitrile. The mixture was stirred to dissolve the solids and cooled to −7°C. To this was slowly added 800 grams, (10.9 moles) of tert-butylamine (commercially available from Aldrich Chemical, Milwaukee, Wis.) at a rate such that the temperature remained below 0°C. (approximately 2.5 hour addition time). The mixture was stirred at −7°C. for one hour and then overnight at room temperature. The solid was collected by filtration, washed with 500 milliliters acetonitrile and dried to give 1,355 grams of (Z)-4-(tert-butylamino)-4-oxo-2-butenoic acid as a white solid.¹³C NMR indicated the product to be 94.62 weight % (Z)-4-(tert-butylamino)-4-oxo-2-butenoic acid, and 5.38 weight % tert-butylamine. This material was used without further purification for the next reaction.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 10 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with maleic anhydride, 0.981 g, 10.0 mmol, and dry toluene, about 20 mL. Add triethylamine, 0.14 mL, 0.1 equiv, and cool the suspension to 0-5 °C. Add tert-butylamine, 1.10 mL, 1.05 equiv, dropwise over 15-30 minutes, optionally diluted with 5 mL toluene. Keep the temperature below 10 °C during addition. After addition, allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for a further 2.5 hours. Monitor consumption of maleic anhydride by TLC, LCMS, or disappearance of anhydride IR bands. If a solid precipitates, filter it, wash with cold toluene, then wash or slurry briefly with cold dilute aqueous HCl adjusted to pH about 2 to liberate the free carboxylic acid from any amine salt. Wash with cold water and dry under vacuum below 40 °C. If no solid precipitates, concentrate the toluene partially, add cold dilute HCl to pH about 2, collect the precipitated product or extract into ethyl acetate as needed, then dry to obtain CC(C)(C)NC(=O)/C=C\C(=O)O. Avoid prolonged heating because maleamic acids can dehydrate or isomerize under harsher conditions.

Collect the precipitated product by filtration if solid forms, or extract the acidified aqueous phase with ethyl acetate or MTBE.

solvents.name: dichloromethane
solvents.volume: 10 mL per 1.00 mmol limiting heteroaryl fluoride

reaction_conditions.time: 3 hours; extend to 6 hours if LCMS/HPLC shows incomplete conversion

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the activated heteroaryl fluoride substrate CC(C)c1cccc(Nc2c(C#N)cnc3cnc(F)cc23)c1, 1.00 equiv, in anhydrous dichloromethane at about 10 mL per mmol of substrate. Add triethylamine, 1.5 equiv, at 20–25 °C. Add 2-morpholinoethylamine, NCCN1CCOCC1, 1.2 equiv, dropwise or portionwise while maintaining the temperature near 25 °C. Stir the reaction at 25 °C for 3 hours and monitor by LCMS or HPLC for consumption of the aryl fluoride. If conversion is incomplete, continue stirring up to 6 hours or warm cautiously to dichloromethane reflux, about 40 °C. After completion, dilute with dichloromethane and wash with water, followed by brine. Dry the organic layer over MgSO4 or Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol containing a small amount of ammonia or triethylamine, or by preparative HPLC if needed, to afford CC(C)c1cccc(Nc2c(C#N)cnc3cnc(NCCN4CCOCC4)cc23)c1.

patent_details: Preparation of 2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-malonic acid dimethyl ester (54): To a solution of anhydrous methanol (250 mL) is added sodium metal (2.875 g, 0.125 mol) piecewise until the evolution of gas has deceased. Dimethyl malonate (16.5 g, 0.125 mol) is added dropwise and the mixture is stirred for 30 minutes. 4-Fluoro benzyl bromide (23.8 g, 0.126 mol) is added dropwise, and the reaction is refluxed for 2 hour. The majority of the solvent is removed under vacuum, and aqueous HCl is added. The solution is extracted with CHCl₃, dried, and the solvent removed in vacuo. Distillation of the crude material under reduced pressure provides the desired compound which is used without further purification.   Preparation of 2-(4-fluorobenxyl)-malonic acid benzyl ester methyl ester (55): Lipozyme (4.0 g) is added to a solution of 2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-malonic acid dimethyl ester, 54, (1.0, 4.7 mmol) and benzyl alcohol (2.9 mL) in hexane (30 mL). The suspension is shaken at 40°C. and 200 rpm. After 18 hours the reaction is filtered, the solvent is removed in vacuo and the crude product purified over silica to afford the desired product which is used without further purification.   Preparation of 2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-malonic acid monomethyl ester (56): 5% Pd/C (64 mg) is added to a solution of 2-(4-fluorobenxyl)-malonic acid benzyl ester methyl ester, 55, (126 mg, 0.4 mmol) in 1:1 hexane/toluene (20 mL). Hydrogenation is carried out at RT until starting material is consumed. The catalyst is removed by filtration, and the solvent removed in vacuo to afford the desired product which is used without further purification.   Preparation of 3-(4-cylcohexyl-4-[1,2,4]triazol-1-ylmethyl-piperidin-1-yl)-2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-3-oxo-propionic acid methyl ester (57): To a solution of 2-(4-fluoro-benzyl)-malonic acid monomethyl ester, 56, (47.5 mg, 0.21 mmol), 4-cyclohexyl-4-[1,2,4]triazol-1-ylmethyl-piperidine, 18, (50 mg, 0.20 mmol), 1-hydroxybenzotriazole (54 mg, 0.40 mmol), 4-methylmorpholine (88 □l, 0.80 mmol) in N,N-dimethylformamide (7 mL) is added 1-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)-3-ethylcarbodiimide (50 mg, 0.26 mmol). The reaction mixture is stirred overnight and then aqueous ammonium chloride is added. The reaction is extracted with ethyl acetate, and the organics are separated dried over sodium sulfate, filtered and concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude product is purified by preparative HPLC to afford the desired compound.   Preparation of 3-(4-cylcohexyl-4-[1,2,4]triazol-1-ylmethyl-piperidin-1-yl)-2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-3-oxo-propionic acid (58): To a solution of 3-(4-cylcohexyl-4-[1,2,4]triazol-1-ylmethyl-piperidin-1-yl)-2-(4-fluorobenzyl)-3-oxo-propionic acid methyl ester, 57, (456 mg, 1 mmol) in THF/H₂O (2:1) at RT is added LiOH (1.5 equiv.). full_recipe.procedure: On a 0.10 mmol scale, dissolve the Boc-protected aryl amine substrate in dichloromethane, ClCCl, 2.0 mL, under nitrogen or air at 0 °C. full_recipe.reaction_name: Regioselective epoxide aminolysis: morpholine ring-opening of a chiral N-glycidyl lactam/oxindole scaffold

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions_summary: Morpholine, ethanol, 70 °C, 16 h
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Best balance of reactivity and substrate compatibility. Ethanol is consistent with the retrieved examples for closely related scaffolds and should solubilize both morpholine and the polar product. Heating is recommended because secondary amine epoxide openings on complex heterocycles can be slow at room temperature.

reagents.name: morpholine
reagents.amount_recommendation: 0.30 mmol, approximately 26 mg or 0.026 mL for a 0.10 mmol substrate scale

full_recipe.procedure: Charge a dry reaction vial with the chiral N-glycidyl epoxide precursor, COc1ccc2c(c1)NC(=O)/C2=C\c1[nH]c2c(c1C)C(=O)N(C[C@H]1CO1)CCC2, as the limiting reagent, for example 0.10 mmol. Add ethanol at approximately 2.0 mL per 0.10 mmol substrate and stir until dissolved or well suspended. Add morpholine, C1COCCN1, 3.0 equivalents, approximately 0.026 mL for a 0.10 mmol scale. Seal the vial or fit with a reflux condenser and heat at 70 °C for 16 hours with stirring. Monitor conversion by LC-MS or TLC. After consumption of the epoxide, cool to room temperature and remove ethanol and excess morpholine under reduced pressure, co-evaporating with toluene if needed. Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol with 0.5-1% triethylamine or by reverse-phase preparative HPLC to afford the target beta-morpholino alcohol: COc1ccc2c(c1)NC(=O)/C2=C\c1[nH]c2c(c1C)C(=O)N(C[C@H](O)CN1CCOCC1)CCC2.

Stir at 0 °C for 30 minutes, then allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for 16 hours or until LC-MS/HPLC shows complete conversion to the sulfone. Quench cautiously with aqueous 1 M NaOH and saturated aqueous sodium thiosulfate, stir for 10 minutes, separate the layers, and extract the aqueous phase with dichloromethane. Wash the combined organic layers with 1 M NaOH, then 1 M HCl if needed, then brine. Dry over sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. After addition, allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for about 2.5 h, monitoring by TLC, GC-MS, LC-MS, or HPLC for disappearance of the alkyne. full_recipe.procedure: In a dry Schlenk tube under nitrogen, charge 1.0 equiv of C=CC(O)(CF)CF and 1.5 equiv of C=Cc1cc(C(F)(F)F)ccc1Cl. Add dry, degassed toluene at 10 mL per mmol of the fluorinated allylic alcohol, followed by tricyclohexylphosphine, 0.05 equiv, and the Grubbs-type Ru catalyst, 0.03 equiv. Seal under nitrogen and heat at 80 °C for 16 hours with stirring. Venting or a gentle nitrogen sweep can help remove ethylene and drive the cross-metathesis. Monitor by TLC, GC-MS, or LC-MS until the fluorinated alkene is consumed. full_recipe.reaction_name: Base-promoted SNAr N-arylation of a secondary piperazine with a chlorocyano fused azaarene

recommendation_and_ranking.recipe: Use the listed reactants with triethylamine in acetonitrile at 80 °C for 16 h.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This is the most direct recommendation for the proposed pathway. The free secondary piperazine nitrogen in the complex Boc-protected amine can displace chloride from the electron-poor chloro-cyano fused azaarene by SNAr to give the target N-aryl piperazine. Acetonitrile is a suitable polar aprotic solvent, and triethylamine can neutralize HCl generated during substitution. A higher temperature than the retrieved 50 °C pyrimidine examples is recommended because the fused chloro azaarene may be less activated than dichloropyrimidine substrates.

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: The closest retrieved SNAr examples use DIPEA in dioxane at 50 °C for piperazine substitution on chloro azaheterocycles in good yields. recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Use the originally proposed amine hydrochloride and aryl phosphorodichloridate in dry dichloromethane with triethylamine. This directly matches the retrieved reaction pattern: an amino ester hydrochloride is coupled with an electrophilic chloride reagent in CH2Cl2 using Et3N, typically beginning at 0 °C and warming to room temperature. The substrate is more moisture-sensitive than ordinary acid/sulfonyl chlorides, so anhydrous solvent, inert atmosphere, slow addition, and excess Et3N are recommended.

A more concentrated room-temperature-only protocol could work by analogy to the sulfonyl chloride example, but it is less preferred because phosphoryl chlorides can react rapidly and exothermically with amines and base, and the target product may be moisture/acid sensitive.

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Best-supported route for the exact substrate class. The retrieved precedent shows the same hydroxy-chromenone core undergoes selective NBS bromination at the same aryl position that becomes methylated in the target. A second retrieved precedent shows aryl bromide-to-aryl methyl conversion using trimethylboroxine/Cs2CO3/Pd(dppf)Cl2. This avoids relying on unsupported direct C-H methylation.

recommendation_and_ranking.option: Direct Friedel-Crafts methylation using a real methyl electrophile such as MeI or MeCl with AlCl3
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This is the closest single-operation interpretation of the proposed AlCl3 condition, but it is much less reliable. The phenol and chromenone carbonyl can strongly bind AlCl3, O-methylation or decomposition may compete, and regioselectivity/yield are uncertain. It requires an added methyl source; AlCl3 alone cannot install a methyl group.

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Not recommended. The product has one additional carbon atom relative to the reactant. full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, dissolve the preserved starting reactant CCOC(=O)N1CCC(c2oc3cc(O)ccc3c(=O)c2C)CC1 in dry DMF at about 0.20 M, using 5.0 mL DMF. Add N-bromosuccinimide, 1.0 equivalent, portionwise at room temperature and stir at 25 °C for 5 hours. Monitor for consumption of starting material and formation of the ortho-brominated phenol intermediate. Dilute with water and extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate. Use the crude or purified aryl bromide intermediate in the next step. For the methylation step, charge the aryl bromide intermediate, 1.0 equivalent, trimethylboroxine, 0.5 equivalent, Cs2CO3, 2.5 equivalents, and Pd(dppf)Cl2, 0.05 equivalent, into a nitrogen-purged flask. Add 1,4-dioxane/water 10:1, using 5.0 mL dioxane and 0.5 mL water per 1.0 mmol intermediate. Degas or purge with nitrogen, then heat at 90 °C for 2 hours. After completion, cool, dilute with water, extract with ethyl acetate, dry, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative RP-HPLC to afford CCOC(=O)N1CCC(c2oc3c(C)c(O)ccc3c(=O)c2C)CC1. The originally proposed AlCl3/CH2Cl2-only condition is not recommended because it lacks a methyl source.

patent_details: 1.4 g of 2-(2,2,3,3,4,4,5,5-octafluoropentyl)malononitrile and 1.0 g of 1-bromo-3-fluoropropane were dissolved in 10 ml of ethylene glycol dimethyl ether, 0.97 g of potassium carbonate was added, and the mixture was stirred at room temperature for 10 hours. Thereafter, dilute hydrochloric acid was added to the reaction mixture, followed by extraction with methyl tert-butyl ether. The organic layer was washed successively with water, aqueous saturated sodium hydrogen carbonate and aqueous saturated sodium chloride, dried over anhydrous magnesium sulfate, and then concentrated under reduced pressure. The residue was subjected to silica gel column chromatography to obtain 0.67 g of 2-(3-fluoropropyl)-2-(2,2,3,3,4,4,5,5-octafluoropentyl)malononitrile (hereinafter, referred to as the present compound (74)).

full_recipe.reaction_name: Sodium-hydride-mediated C-alkylation of a substituted malononitrile with 1-fluoro-3-iodopropane

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions_summary: Use NaH in anhydrous DMF, add 1-fluoro-3-iodopropane at 0 °C, then stir at 25 °C.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Best match to the proposed pathway and retrieved precedent #3, where a substituted malononitrile is deprotonated with NaH in DMF and alkylated with a primary haloalkane. The target transformation is a straightforward SN2 C-alkylation of the acidic malononitrile methine. The electrophile FCCCI is a primary iodide, so it should react efficiently while retaining the terminal C-F bond.

reagents.name: sodium hydride, preferably 60% dispersion in mineral oil

procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, charge a dry flask with 2-(2,2,3,3,4,4,5,5-octafluoropentyl)malononitrile, 1.00 equiv, and anhydrous DMF, 5.0 mL per mmol of substrate.
Cool the solution to 0 °C and add sodium hydride, 1.10 equiv, portionwise. Maintain 0 °C during addition and allow gas evolution to subside.
Stir at 0 °C for 30 minutes to form the malononitrile anion.
Add 1-fluoro-3-iodopropane, 1.30 equiv, dropwise at 0 °C.
Warm the reaction mixture to 25 °C and stir for 5 hours. Monitor by TLC, GC-MS, or LC-MS for consumption of the starting malononitrile.
Cool to 0 °C and cautiously quench remaining NaH with saturated aqueous NH4Cl or dilute hydrochloric acid, added slowly.
Dilute with water and extract with methyl tert-butyl ether or ethyl acetate.
Wash the organic layer with water, saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate, and brine; dry over anhydrous MgSO4 or Na2SO4.
Filter, concentrate under reduced pressure, and purify the residue by silica gel column chromatography to obtain N#CC(C#N)(CCCF)CC(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)(F)C(F)F.
Safety note: avoid heating NaH/DMF mixtures; keep the reaction near room temperature and quench carefully because hydrogen gas is evolved.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Reductive amination / N-alkylation of methylindoline with isovanillin using sodium triacetoxyborohydride

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: Sodium triacetoxyborohydride in dichloromethane, 0 °C addition then room temperature
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This is the best-matched condition set. The target transformation is a reductive amination between the aldehyde of isovanillin and the secondary amine of a methylindoline, giving the tertiary benzylated indoline. The retrieved examples are essentially direct analogues: isovanillin plus methylindoline regioisomers using sodium triacetoxyborohydride in dichloromethane, producing the corresponding N-benzyl indolines in 51–62% yield. Sodium triacetoxyborohydride is appropriate because it selectively reduces iminium intermediates under mildly acidic/neutral conditions and is compatible with phenols and anisoles.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or dry air, dissolve isovanillin, COc1ccc(C=O)cc1O, 1.0 equiv, and the methylindoline substrate, Cc1cccc2c1NCC2, 1.0 equiv, in dichloromethane at approximately 5.0 mL per mmol of limiting reactant. Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add sodium triacetoxyborohydride, 1.0 equiv, portionwise while maintaining the temperature near 0 °C. Stir for 10 minutes at 0 °C, then allow the reaction to warm to 23 °C and stir for approximately 5 hours. Monitor by TLC or LCMS for consumption of aldehyde and formation of the tertiary amine product. Quench by pouring the reaction into ice-cold saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate. Separate the organic layer and extract the aqueous phase with dichloromethane. Combine organic layers, wash with brine, dry over magnesium sulfate or sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude material by flash chromatography on silica gel, for example using hexane/ethyl acetate or hexane/MTBE gradient, to obtain COc1ccc(CN2CCc3cccc(C)c32)cc1O.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, charge a flask with the chiral aryl azide trifluoroacetamide, 4-phenyl-1-butyne / phenethyl acetylene component (1.20 equiv), sodium ascorbate represented by the ascorbate anion plus sodium counterion (0.20 equiv), CuI (0.05 equiv), tert-butanol (5.0 mL), and water (5.0 mL). Dilute with ethyl acetate and water, separate the layers, and extract the aqueous phase with ethyl acetate. procedure: On a 0.50 mmol scale, charge a flask with the chiral aryl azide, 1.00 equiv, and C#CCCc1ccccc1, 1.20 equiv.
Add tert-butanol, 2.5 mL, and water, 2.5 mL, to give an approximately 0.1 M reaction mixture with respect to the aryl azide.
Add sodium ascorbate, 0.20 equiv, followed by CuSO4·5H2O, 0.05 equiv. The CuSO4/sodium ascorbate system generates the active Cu(I) catalyst in situ.
Stir the reaction at 25 °C for 16 hours. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC for disappearance of the aryl azide/alkyne.
If incomplete after 16 hours, add an additional 0.05 equiv sodium ascorbate and stir for a further 4-8 hours, optionally warming to 35-40 °C.
After completion, dilute with ethyl acetate and wash with aqueous EDTA or dilute ammonium hydroxide solution to remove copper salts, then wash with water and brine.
Dry the organic layer over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford CC[C@H](NC(=O)C(F)(F)F)c1ccc(-n2cc(CCc3ccccc3)nn2)cc1.

full_recipe.procedure: In a sealed 10 mL reaction vial equipped with a stir bar, charge N-[(1S)-1-(4-iodophenyl)propyl]-2,2,2-trifluoroacetamide, 4-phenylbut-1-yne, sodium azide, sodium ascorbate, and copper(II) sulfate. Monitor by LCMS for disappearance of the aryl iodide and formation of the triazole product. After cooling, dilute with ethyl acetate, filter through Celite if copper solids are present, and wash the organic layer with aqueous EDTA or ammonia solution, water, and brine. Dry over sodium sulfate, concentrate, and purify by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain CC[C@H](NC(=O)C(F)(F)F)c1ccc(-n2cc(CCc3ccccc3)nn2)cc1. Use appropriate azide safety precautions and avoid acidifying sodium azide-containing mixtures.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve CC(C)(C)OC(=O)C[C@H](OC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)O, 1.00 equiv, and N-hydroxysuccinimide, 1.10 equiv, in anhydrous THF, using about 10 mL THF per 1.00 mmol acid substrate. full_recipe.procedure: Under an argon or nitrogen atmosphere, dissolve the N-benzenesulfonyl protected precursor, 1.0 equivalent, in anhydrous THF at approximately 0.10–0.13 M, using about 8 mL THF per 1.0 mmol substrate. Cool the solution to 0 °C in an ice bath. Add tetrabutylammonium fluoride, preferably as a 1.0 M solution in THF, 2.2 equivalents, dropwise while maintaining 0 °C. Stir at 0 °C for 1 hour and monitor by LCMS or TLC for disappearance of starting material and formation of the N-H product. If incomplete, allow the mixture to warm to 20–25 °C and stir for an additional 1–2 hours. Quench carefully with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride, about 5 mL per 1.0 mmol substrate. Extract with ethyl acetate, 3 portions of about 15 mL per 1.0 mmol substrate. Wash the combined organic layers with brine, dry over anhydrous magnesium sulfate or sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography, for example n-hexane/ethyl acetate from 3:1 to 1:1, to afford the target free N-H product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: TBAF-mediated N-tosyl deprotection of an indole to the corresponding NH indole

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: Tetrabutylammonium fluoride, 1.0 M in THF, 3.0 equiv; dry THF; 0 °C to 25 °C; 3 h total
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Best recommendation for the proposed pathway. The local reactant is an N-tosyl-protected indole and the product is the corresponding free NH indole, with all other scaffold connectivity conserved. TBAF in THF is a plausible reagent system for desulfonylation of N-sulfonyl indoles under mild conditions. The retrieved examples strongly support the compatibility of TBAF/THF with the same methyl pyridine-carboxylate/benzylic alcohol/aryl heterocycle scaffold, although those examples are desilylations rather than N-tosyl deprotections. Starting cold minimizes side reactions involving the methyl ester or benzylic alcohol, then warming to room temperature improves conversion.

Seal or fit with a reflux condenser under nitrogen and heat at 100 °C for 16 hours with stirring. Monitor by LCMS or TLC for consumption of aminopyridine/aldehyde and formation of the desired [M+H]+ product. Cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and carefully quench with saturated aqueous NaHCO3 while controlling gas evolution. Separate the organic phase, extract the aqueous phase with ethyl acetate, combine the organic layers, wash with brine, dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude material by flash chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain the target product. Safety note: perchloric acid in organic media is hazardous; use only catalytic quantities, avoid dryness/heating of residues containing perchlorate, and conduct the reaction behind a blast shield in a properly rated hood.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol substrate scale, charge a well-ventilated fume-hood reactor with bromine, 5.0 equiv, in water, 1.2 mL, and cool to 0 °C. full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry reaction vial with the imino azaheterocyclic [nH] nucleophile, Cn1c(=N)[nH]c2nc(-c3ccccc3C(F)(F)F)ncc21, 1.0 equiv, and the aryl methyl bromide electrophile, CCn1cc(C(F)(F)F)nc1-c1ccc(CBr)cc1, 1.05 equiv. Add dry DMF at about 2.0 mL per 0.100 mmol of limiting nucleophile. Add finely powdered Cs2CO3, 2.0 equiv, at 25 °C. Stir the suspension at 25 °C for 20 hours and monitor conversion by LC-MS or HPLC. After completion, dilute with ethyl acetate and quench with water or saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate. Separate the layers, extract the aqueous phase with ethyl acetate, combine the organic layers, wash with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4 or MgSO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol or ethyl acetate/hexanes with a small amount of base modifier if needed to afford the target N-benzylated product.

recommendation_and_ranking.recipe: Use the original reactants with HATU and DIPEA in anhydrous DMF at 25 °C for 1 h.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This is a direct carboxylic acid-to-amide coupling. The local reactant scaffold pre-check passed, and the product is obtained by replacing the acid OH with the chiral oxabicyclic amine while conserving all non-reacting scaffold connectivity, deuteration, aryl substituents, chlorine, and stereochemistry. HATU/DIPEA is strongly supported by the two closest retrieved examples, which use the same chiral amine hydrochloride and closely related imidazo-pyridazine carboxylic acids.

Prepare a concentrated aqueous solution of sodium nitrite in a portion of the water and add it dropwise over about 5 minutes while maintaining 20-25 °C. Stir for 30 minutes to form the diazonium intermediate. Prepare a concentrated aqueous solution of potassium iodide in the remaining reagent water and add it dropwise over about 5 minutes. If iodine color is present, add aqueous sodium thiosulfate and stir for 30 minutes until the iodine color disappears. Collect the precipitated product by filtration, wash thoroughly with water, and dry under vacuum or nitrogen. If needed, purify by trituration or preparative chromatography to obtain O=C1Nc2ncccc2[C@]12Cc1ccc(I)cc1C2.

Stir at 20 °C until consumption of starting material is observed, typically overnight, about 12–16 hours total. Extract with ethyl acetate or concentrate and purify directly depending on solubility. Wash organic layers with brine, dry over sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude material by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol with a small amount of acetic acid or by reverse-phase chromatography to afford the target phosphinic pseudopeptide product.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, charge a dry reaction flask with NC1CC(=O)NC1=O, potassium carbonate, and anhydrous acetonitrile under nitrogen. Add 1-bromononane, preferably dropwise or in one portion with efficient stirring. Heat the heterogeneous mixture at reflux, approximately 82 °C, for 16 hours. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC for consumption of the aminopiperidinedione starting material and formation of the dialkylated product. Partition the residue between ethyl acetate and water, separate the organic phase, and wash with brine. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude material by silica gel chromatography using a gradient such as dichloromethane/methanol with a small amount of ammonium hydroxide or triethylamine to suppress tailing of the amine-containing product.

Working up of the mixture was carried out by separating off the urea which had precipitated out and introducing the filtrate into a mixture of saturated NaCl solution (40 ml) and saturated NaHCO₃ solution (10 ml). Still further urea thereby precipitated out and was separated off. 5 M sodium hydroxide solution (4 ml, 20 mmol) was added to the aqueous phase and the mixture was diluted with water (300 ml) and stored at 5°C. for 3 d. The product thereby precipitated out as a colourless solid in a yield of 65% (227 mg) and with an m.p. of 145-148°C.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.0 mmol scale, place N-(1H-indol-7-yl)methanesulfonamide, 1.0 equiv, and 3-(4-methylphenyl)pentan-3-ol, 1.0 equiv, in a dry flask under nitrogen. procedure: Under a nitrogen atmosphere, charge a dry reaction flask with N-(1H-indolyl)methanesulfonamide, CS(=O)(=O)Nc1cccc2cc[nH]c12, 1.00 mmol, 1.0 equiv, approximately 210 mg.
Add 3-(4-methylphenyl)pentan-3-ol, CCC(O)(CC)c1ccc(C)cc1, 1.00 mmol, 1.0 equiv, approximately 178 mg or about 0.18 mL.
Add dry dichloromethane, ClCCl, 10.0 mL, to give an approximately 0.10 M reaction mixture.
Add trifluoroacetic acid, O=C(O)C(F)(F)F, 1.50 mmol, 1.5 equiv, approximately 0.115 mL, at room temperature.
Stir the reaction mixture at 22 °C under nitrogen for 18 h. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC for consumption of the indole starting material and formation of the higher-mass C3-alkylated product.
Quench carefully by adding saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate slowly, allowing CO2 evolution to subside. For a 1 mmol scale, use approximately 30-50 mL saturated NaHCO3.
Extract the mixture with ethyl acetate, approximately 3 x 25 mL. Combine the organic layers, wash with brine, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.

Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography, for example using an ethyl acetate/hexanes gradient starting around 30% ethyl acetate and increasing to 70% ethyl acetate as needed, to afford CCC(CC)(c1ccc(C)cc1)c1c[nH]c2c(NS(C)(=O)=O)cccc12.

Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add N,N-diisopropylethylamine, followed by slow dropwise addition of chloromethyl methyl ether. Cool to 0 °C. Add sodium hydride, 1.5 equiv, portionwise while maintaining the temperature at 0 °C and allowing hydrogen evolution to remain controlled. Stir at 0 °C for 20 min, then warm to 25 °C and stir for 1 h to form the alkoxide mixture. Add the polyunsaturated fatty alcohol, CCCCC/C=C\C/C=C\CCCCCCCCO, 1.2 equiv, preferably as a solution in a small amount of dry THF. Heat the reaction at 60 °C for 16 h under nitrogen. Monitor by LC-MS, TLC, or HPLC. Cool to 0 °C and cautiously quench residual NaH with slow addition of isopropanol or methanol, followed by water. Extract with ethyl acetate or hexane/ethyl acetate, wash the organic layer with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify by silica gel chromatography using a nonpolar eluent such as hexane/ethyl acetate. Important caution: because no alkyl halide, sulfonate ester, or other leaving group is present, formation of the target ether is expected to be poor or absent under these exact conditions.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Acid-promoted dehydrative etherification of a fatty alcohol with a chiral hydroxy ether

recommendation_and_ranking.rational: Use the locally proposed reactants unchanged and attempt p-toluenesulfonic-acid-promoted intermolecular etherification in dry THF at reflux. This preserves the target scaffold: the free hydroxymethyl group of the chiral mono-ether can formally couple with the long-chain dienyl alcohol to give the observed diether. However, direct etherification of two unactivated alcohols is intrinsically difficult and the presence of sodium hydride together with p-toluenesulfonic acid is chemically antagonistic, so this is a constrained, low-confidence recommendation.

The retrieved examples strongly support a Williamson ether synthesis manifold: alcohol deprotonation with NaH followed by reaction with an alkyl bromide or other activated electrophile, typically in DMF at 60-100 °C. That would likely be more reliable if the fatty alcohol were first converted to a tosylate, mesylate, bromide, or iodide. This is not selected as the main recommendation because the local reactant scaffold pre-check passed and the original reactants must be preserved.

reaction_conditions.concentration: 0.10 M with respect to chloropyrimidinamine substrate
reaction_conditions.atmosphere: Nitrogen or argon preferred; sealed pressure tube recommended

procedure: Charge a dry sealed tube with Nc1nccc(Cl)n1, the chloropyrimidinamine substrate, 1.00 equiv, 1.00 mmol, and a stir bar.
Add ethanol, 10.0 mL, followed by N-methyl-2-fluoroethanamine, CNCCF, 1.50 equiv, and triethylamine, CCN(CC)CC, 2.00 equiv.

Extract with ethyl acetate or 4:1 dichloromethane/isopropanol. Wash the combined organic layers with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate.

reagents.volume: use as a freshly prepared or commercial solution; for a 0.5 M solution use 2.20 mL

full_recipe.procedure: In an oven-dried Schlenk flask or glovebox-compatible vessel equipped with a stir bar, charge the tetramethylcyclopentadienyl-triphenylsilyl titanium trichloride ion-pair precursor, CC1=C(C)[C]([Ti+3])([Si](c2ccccc2)(c2ccccc2)c2ccccc2)C(C)=C1C.[Cl-].[Cl-].[Cl-], as 1.00 equiv under nitrogen or argon. Add dry THF, 15.0 mL per mmol of precursor, followed by dry hexane, 10.0 mL per mmol, to give a stirred suspension or solution. Cool the mixture to -78 °C. Add phenyllithium, [Li][c]1ccccc1, 1.05 equiv, dropwise over 30 minutes while maintaining the internal temperature at -78 °C. Stir for an additional 30 minutes at -78 °C. In a separate dry vessel, prepare or measure a solution of chlorotrimethyltitanium, [CH3][Ti]([CH3])([CH3])[Cl], 1.10 equiv, in dry diethyl ether, approximately 5.0 mL per mmol of precursor, or use the stated commercial concentration. Add this solution dropwise to the cold reaction mixture over 30 minutes at -78 °C. Allow the reaction mixture to warm gradually to 23 °C over 2 hours, then stir at 23 °C for 12 hours. Remove insoluble lithium salts and titanium byproducts by filtration through a dry, inert-atmosphere cannula filter or a pad of dry Celite under nitrogen. Rinse the solids with dry hexane. Concentrate the combined filtrates under reduced pressure at low temperature. Purify the crude organotitanium product by extraction with dry hexane and crystallization from hexane/ether at -30 °C, maintaining exclusion of air and moisture throughout.

procedure: Charge a dry reaction flask with CN(C)CCNc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)NC2(CF)CC2)cc1, using 1.00 mmol as the limiting substrate.
Cool the flask in an ice bath and add concentrated sulfuric acid, 5.0 mL per 1.00 mmol substrate, slowly with stirring. Maintain the internal temperature at 0-5 °C.
Add 70 wt% nitric acid, 1.10 equivalents, dropwise over 0.25 h while keeping the internal temperature at or below 5 °C.

After addition, stir at 0 °C for 0.50 h, then allow the mixture to warm to 20 °C and stir for 1.50 h. Monitor by LCMS or HPLC for consumption of starting material and formation of the mononitrated product.
When complete, carefully pour the reaction mixture onto crushed ice with vigorous stirring, keeping the quench temperature below 10 °C.

Slowly adjust the aqueous mixture to pH 8.5-9.0 with cold aqueous sodium hydroxide or sodium carbonate solution. Avoid strongly basic conditions for prolonged time to minimize sulfonamide ionization and product loss to the aqueous phase.

Extract with dichloromethane or ethyl acetate. If extraction is poor, use dichloromethane/methanol 95:5. Wash the combined organic layers with brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.

Purify the crude material by silica gel chromatography using dichloromethane/methanol with a small amount of ammonium hydroxide or by preparative HPLC to afford CN(C)CCNc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)NC2(CF)CC2)cc1[N+](=O)[O-].

procedure: Dry a round-bottom flask, fit it with a nitrogen inlet, magnetic stir bar, septum, and addition funnel or syringe-access port.
Charge the flask with 5-chloro-2-nitrobenzaldehyde, diethyl malonate, and anhydrous toluene. Stir under nitrogen until a suspension or solution is obtained.
Cool the mixture to 0 °C in an ice bath.
Add TiCl4 slowly dropwise, maintaining the internal temperature near 0–5 °C. TiCl4 is moisture-sensitive and strongly fuming; add under inert atmosphere.
Add pyridine slowly at 0–5 °C. A precipitate or darkening may occur due to pyridinium/titanium salts.
Remove the ice bath and stir at 25 °C for 16 h. Monitor conversion by TLC, LCMS, or HPLC. If incomplete, warm to 50 °C for an additional 2–4 h.
Cool the reaction to 0 °C and cautiously quench by slow addition into stirred ice-cold 1 M HCl or saturated NH4Cl. Keep the temperature controlled because hydrolysis of titanium salts is exothermic.
Extract with ethyl acetate, filter through Celite if titanium solids are present, and separate the organic layer.
Wash the organic layer with water, saturated NaHCO3 if needed, then brine. Dry over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the crude diethyl 2-(5-chloro-2-nitrobenzylidene)malonate by silica gel chromatography or crystallization from ethanol/heptane, depending on crude purity.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 10 mmol scale, charge a dry round-bottom flask fitted with a Dean-Stark trap and condenser with 5-chloro-2-nitrobenzaldehyde, diethyl malonate, and toluene. Add pyrrolidine followed by acetic acid. Heat the mixture to reflux at about 110 °C with azeotropic removal of water for 6 hours, monitoring by TLC or LCMS until the aldehyde is consumed. Cool to room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, and wash sequentially with saturated aqueous NH4Cl, saturated NaHCO3 or K2HPO4 solution, and brine. Dry the organic phase over Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the crude product by recrystallization from ethanol/heptane or by silica gel chromatography to afford diethyl 2-[(5-chloro-2-nitrophenyl)methylene]malonate.

full_recipe.reaction_name: NBS bromination of a furyl acrylate derivative

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, flame-dry or oven-dry a reaction flask, equip it with a stir bar, and maintain under nitrogen or argon. Dissolve the chiral bislactim ether substrate, COC1=N[C@H](C(C)C)C(OC)=NC1, 1.00 equiv, in anhydrous THF, 10 mL, and cool to -78 °C. Add n-butyllithium, [Li][CH2]CCC, 1.10 equiv, dropwise while maintaining -78 °C. Stir for 30 min at -78 °C to form the lithiated bislactim intermediate. Add a solution of the alkyl triflate, O=S(=O)(OCCC(c1ccccc1)C(F)(F)F)C(F)(F)F, 1.10 equiv, in a small additional portion of anhydrous THF if needed, dropwise at -78 °C. Stir for 1 h at -78 °C, then allow the reaction to warm slowly to 0 °C over approximately 2 h. Monitor conversion by TLC or LCMS. Quench carefully at 0 °C with saturated aqueous NH4Cl, approximately 5 equiv or 5–10 mL per mmol substrate. Allow the mixture to reach room temperature, dilute with ethyl acetate, separate the layers, and extract the aqueous layer with ethyl acetate. Combine the organic layers, wash with brine, dry over MgSO4 or Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography using a nonpolar-to-moderately polar eluent such as heptane/ethyl acetate to afford COC1=N[C@H](C(C)C)C(OC)=N[C@H]1CCC(c1ccccc1)C(F)(F)F.

reaction_conditions.time: 3 hours total: approximately 0.5 hours at 0 °C followed by 2.5 hours at 25 °C

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the aniline-containing dihydropyridine precursor, 1.0 equiv, in dry dichloromethane, approximately 15 mL per 1.0 mmol substrate. Cool the solution to 0 °C and add pyridine, 2.5 equiv. Add triflic anhydride, 1.1 equiv, dropwise at 0 °C while maintaining the internal temperature below 5 °C. Stir for 30 minutes at 0 °C, then allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for an additional 2.5 hours. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC for consumption of the aniline precursor and formation of the mono-triflylated product. Quench carefully at 0 °C with cold water. Separate the organic phase and wash with dilute aqueous HCl to remove pyridine, then with brine. Dry the organic layer over anhydrous MgSO4 or Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography using a dichloromethane/ethyl acetate or hexane/ethyl acetate gradient, avoiding strongly basic aqueous washes because the aryl triflamide N-H can be acidic and may partition into aqueous base.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, dissolve the N-H pyridone precursor in anhydrous DMF at about 0.05 M concentration, using 2.0 mL DMF for a 0.10 mmol scale. Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add sodium hydride, 1.2 equivalents, portionwise while maintaining 0 °C, and stir for 20 minutes to form the pyridone/lactam anion. Add iodomethane, 1.5 equivalents, dropwise at 0 °C. Allow the reaction mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 3 hours, monitoring by LC-MS or HPLC for disappearance of starting material and formation of the N-methyl product. Quench carefully at 0 °C with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride or methanol followed by water. Dilute with ethyl acetate, wash with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by reversed-phase preparative HPLC or silica chromatography using a suitable gradient to isolate the target N-methyl pyridone product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Williamson-type phenolic O-alkylation with a chloromethyl N-methylpyridone

recommendation_and_ranking.recommended_conditions: Use the local reactants as provided: phenolic precursor, chloromethyl N-methylpyridone, and K2CO3 in dry DMF at 60 °C for 24 h.

reaction_conditions.time: 24 h; extend to 48 h if LCMS shows incomplete conversion

full_recipe.procedure: On a 0.10 mmol scale, charge a sealed reaction vial with the phenolic precursor, chloromethyl N-methylpyridone electrophile, and finely powdered potassium carbonate. Add dry DMF at about 1.8 mL per 0.10 mmol phenolic precursor. Seal the vial and heat with stirring or shaking at 60 °C for 24 h. Monitor by LCMS for disappearance of the phenol and formation of the desired O-alkylated product. If incomplete, continue heating at 60 °C up to 48 h. Cool to room temperature, dilute with DMF, MeOH, or DMSO as needed, remove inorganic solids by filtration, and purify directly by reversed-phase preparative HPLC. Alternatively, dilute with water, extract with ethyl acetate, dry, concentrate, and purify by chromatography if compatible with the product. Use ethyl acetate for workup/purification rather than as the main reaction solvent.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Suzuki-Miyaura biaryl cross-coupling

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions_summary: Pd(dppf)Cl2-catalyzed Suzuki coupling of the complex aryl boronic acid with the 1-bromo-2,6-dimethyl-4-alkoxybenzene partner using K2CO3 in toluene/water under nitrogen.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This directly forms the target biaryl C(sp2)-C(sp2) bond. The retrieved closest precedent uses the same complex benzofuran/indane scaffold and a dimethyl aryl boronate/bromide Suzuki coupling with Pd(dppf)Cl2 and carbonate base in toluene at elevated temperature. K2CO3/toluene/water is a standard compatible system for aryl bromide/aryl boronic acid couplings and avoids strongly basic conditions that could hydrolyze the methyl ester.

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions_summary: Microwave Suzuki coupling using Pd(dppf)Cl2, optional dppf, Cs2CO3, toluene, 120 °C, 1.5 h.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This is almost directly supported by the retrieved example on the same core scaffold. It may be faster and effective for hindered 2,6-dimethyl aryl systems, but uses harsher base and microwave heating.

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions_summary: K2CO3 in toluene/water without palladium catalyst.
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Not recommended. Carbonate base alone cannot mediate the required aryl-aryl bond formation from an aryl bromide and boronic acid/boronate ester.

Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography or preparative reverse-phase HPLC to afford the target Suzuki-coupled biaryl product.

The stirring was continued at 0°C. for 30 minutes and then at ambient temperature for one hour. solvents.volume: 6 mL per 1 mmol amine scale, used for acid chloride formation

solvents.name: N,N-dimethylacetamide, anhydrous

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve 1-methyl-1H-pyrrole-2-carboxylic acid, 1.5 equiv, in anhydrous THF, approximately 6 mL per 1 mmol of amine planned. Add catalytic DMF, then add oxalyl chloride, 3.0 equiv relative to amine, dropwise at 20-25 °C. Stir for 1 hour until gas evolution subsides. Remove THF and excess oxalyl chloride under reduced pressure to give the crude acid chloride. Co-evaporate once with dry THF if necessary to remove residual oxalyl chloride. Dissolve the crude acid chloride in anhydrous DMA, approximately 4 mL per 1 mmol amine. Separately dissolve or suspend the aminophenoxy heteroaryl amine, 1.0 equiv, in anhydrous DMA, approximately 4 mL per 1 mmol amine, and cool to 0 °C. Add the acid chloride solution slowly at 0 °C, then allow the mixture to warm to 20-25 °C and stir for 15 hours. Quench by adding water or saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate cautiously, extract with ethyl acetate, wash the organic layer with water and brine, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify by silica or NH-silica gel chromatography using ethyl acetate/hexane or ethyl acetate-rich conditions, followed if needed by trituration or recrystallization from ethyl acetate/hexane.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry reaction vessel with the iodinated heteroaryl cyclopropanecarboxamide, 1.0 equiv, the phenolic amide, 1.1 equiv, and finely powdered potassium carbonate, 2.0 equiv. Add anhydrous DMF, about 5.0 mL per 0.20 mmol of iodinated substrate, and stir the suspension at room temperature for 10 minutes. Heat to 80 °C and stir for 12 hours, monitoring by LC-MS or HPLC for consumption of the aryl iodide. After completion, cool to room temperature, dilute with water, and extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the residue by silica gel or NH-silica chromatography using ethyl acetate/methanol or dichloromethane/methanol as appropriate, followed by trituration or recrystallization from ethyl acetate if needed to afford the target aryl ether product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: EDC/HOBt-mediated amide coupling of 1-methyl-1H-pyrrole-2-carboxylic acid with an aniline

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: A retrieved precedent uses the same 1-methylpyrrole-carboxylic acid acyl fragment, but the reported yield was low, about 14%, and acid chlorides of heteroaryl carboxylic acids can be less robust. This is a viable backup only if carbodiimide coupling fails.

recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Chemically plausible for aniline amidation, but not directly supported by the retrieved examples for this exact scaffold. Consider only as optimization.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, charge a dry flask with the aniline substrate, Nc1cccc(Oc2ccc3nc(NC(=O)C4CC4)cn3n2)c1, 1.00 equiv, and 1-methyl-1H-pyrrole-2-carboxylic acid, Cn1cccc1C(=O)O, 1.05 equiv. After completion, dilute with water, extract with ethyl acetate, wash the organic phase with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4 or MgSO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify the residue by silica or NH-silica chromatography, for example ethyl acetate/hexane followed by ethyl acetate/methanol if needed, to afford Cn1cccc1C(=O)Nc1cccc(Oc2ccc3nc(NC(=O)C4CC4)cn3n2)c1.

procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, charge a dry flask with 1-methyl-1H-pyrrole-2-carboxylic acid, HOBt, and anhydrous DMF.
Cool the mixture to 0 °C and add DIPEA, followed by EDC.HCl portionwise. Stir at 0 °C for 30 min to generate the activated ester in situ.
Add the aniline coupling partner as a solution or suspension in a small portion of DMF. Allow the reaction mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 16 h.
Monitor conversion by LCMS or HPLC. If starting aniline remains, add an additional 0.3 equiv EDC.HCl and 0.3 equiv HOBt and stir for a further 4-8 h at 25 °C.

Dilute the reaction with water and saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate, then extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.

Purify the residue by silica gel or NH-silica chromatography using ethyl acetate/hexane or dichloromethane/methanol mixtures, then triturate or recrystallize from ethyl acetate/hexane if needed to obtain the target amide.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Boron trichloride-mediated debenzylation of aryl benzyl ethers to resorcinol

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: BCl3, anhydrous dichloromethane, N2, 0 °C addition and short stirring at 0 °C to room temperature
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This is the most directly supported condition set. The target transformation is cleavage of two aryl benzyl ether protecting groups to give the corresponding chlorinated resorcinol while retaining the isoxazole core and the p-anisyl methoxy group. The closest retrieved precedent is essentially the bromo analogue of the same isoxazole scaffold using BCl3 in CH2Cl2 to give the bis-phenol. A second precedent shows the chloro bis-benzyloxy aryl system also undergoes clean BCl3 debenzylation under cold conditions. Use controlled low temperature and moderate excess BCl3 to minimize undesired cleavage of the anisole methyl ether.

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: BCl3, anhydrous dichloromethane, room temperature, 1 h
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Also strongly precedent-backed by the closest bromo-isoxazole example, but slightly less preferred because room-temperature BCl3 may increase risk of over-cleavage or decomposition, especially with the retained aryl methyl ether.

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: Hydrogenolysis or transfer hydrogenation conditions
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: General benzyl ether removal is possible, but the retrieved hydrogen-transfer example on a related scaffold gave rearranged/cyclized chromenone-type product rather than the desired simple bis-phenol. Therefore it is not recommended for this exact target.

full_recipe.reaction_name: BCl3-mediated O-benzyl aryl ether deprotection to phenol

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: Boron trichloride in anhydrous dichloromethane under nitrogen at 0 °C
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: This is the best match to the retrieved precedents. Closely related aryl-isoxazole and aryl-pyrazole substrates bearing benzyloxy-protected chlorinated/brominated resorcinol motifs were cleanly debenzylated with BCl3 in CH2Cl2 while retaining the para-methoxyphenyl group. The target transformation is a single O-benzyl cleavage to a phenol, so BCl3/DCM at low temperature is strongly supported. Use controlled low temperature and limited time to reduce risk of anisole demethylation.

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: TFA/thioanisole acidolysis
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: TFA with thioanisole can sometimes cleave benzyl-type protecting groups by acidolysis with thioanisole acting as a cation scavenger. However, simple aryl benzyl ethers are usually less reliably cleaved than PMB or highly activated benzyl ethers. The proposed solvent 'CO' is chemically implausible as a practical solvent notation here. This is a possible but less-preferred backup condition.

recommendation_and_ranking.conditions: Catalytic hydrogenolysis, e.g. H2/Pd-C
recommendation_and_ranking.rationale: Hydrogenolysis is a standard method for O-benzyl deprotection, but this substrate contains an aryl chloride and an isoxazole, both of which may be sensitive to reduction or dehalogenation under hydrogenation conditions. Therefore it is less attractive than the Lewis-acid precedent.

After completion, remove volatile solvent and excess HCl under reduced pressure. procedure: Under nitrogen or dry air, charge a dry reaction vessel with the phenolic aryl pyrimidinedione substrate, O=c1cc(C(F)(F)F)[nH]c(=O)n1-c1cc(Oc2ccccc2O)c(Cl)cc1F, 1.00 equivalent.
Add dry N,N-dimethylformamide, CN(C)C=O, using approximately 20 mL per 1.00 mmol of phenolic substrate.
Add finely powdered potassium carbonate, O=C([O-])[O-].[K+].[K+], 1.5 equivalents, and stir for 10 minutes at 25 °C.
Add ethyl bromoacetate, CCOC(=O)CBr, 1.1 equivalents, preferably dropwise or in one portion at 25 °C.
Stir the mixture at 25 °C for 12 hours and monitor by LC-MS or TLC. The desired conversion is formation of the mono-O-alkylated ethyl aryloxyacetate while retaining the pyrimidinedione [nH].
If incomplete after 12 hours, add an additional 0.1 equivalent of ethyl bromoacetate and continue stirring for 2-4 hours, avoiding large excess to minimize N-alkylation.

Quench by pouring the reaction mixture into ice-water. Adjust cautiously to mildly acidic pH, approximately pH 5-6, with dilute hydrochloric acid if needed to dissolve inorganic carbonate and neutralize salts.
Extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over anhydrous MgSO4 or Na2SO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure.
Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography, for example dichloromethane/ethyl acetate gradient, to afford CCOC(=O)COc1ccccc1Oc1cc(-n2c(=O)cc(C(F)(F)F)[nH]c2=O)c(F)cc1Cl.

Add a solution of the aryl isocyanate, 1.00 mmol, in anhydrous DMF, 3 mL, dropwise at 0 °C. Allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 16 h. Monitor consumption of the aryl isocyanate and formation of the uracil product by LC-MS or HPLC. When complete, slowly pour the reaction mixture into stirred ice-water containing dilute hydrochloric acid to pH about 2-3, maintaining external cooling. Collect the precipitated solid if formed or extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the organic layer with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative reverse-phase HPLC to obtain CCOC(=O)COc1ccccc1Oc1cc(-n2c(=O)cc(C(F)(F)F)[nH]c2=O)c(F)cc1Cl.

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen, dissolve the lactam precursor O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N1CCC(n2c(=O)[nH]c3ccccc32)C1, 1.0 equiv, in dry DMF at about 5.0 mL per mmol. Cool the solution to 0 °C. Add sodium hydride, 60% dispersion in mineral oil, 1.3 equiv, portionwise while maintaining 0 °C. Stir at 0 °C for 30 minutes to form the sodium lactam anion. Add methyl 4-(bromomethyl)-3-fluorobenzoate, 1.05 equiv, preferably as a solution in a small amount of dry DMF. Allow the reaction mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 2-3 hours, monitoring by LC-MS or HPLC for consumption of starting material. Carefully quench the reaction at 0-25 °C by slow addition of water. Dilute with ethyl acetate, separate the layers, and extract the aqueous phase with ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with water and saturated brine, dry over anhydrous Na2SO4 or MgSO4, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the crude residue by silica gel chromatography, for example ethyl acetate/hexane gradient from 0% to 50% ethyl acetate, to afford the target N-benzylated product.

full_recipe.reaction_name: Acid-catalyzed Fischer esterification of substituted fluorobenzoic acid to methyl ester

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, charge a dry round-bottom flask with the substituted fluorobenzoic acid precursor and methanol, using approximately 10.0 mL of methanol. Stir to dissolve or suspend the material. Add concentrated sulfuric acid slowly, approximately 0.20 equivalents, corresponding to about 0.011 mL on this scale. Heat the mixture at methanol reflux, about 65 °C, for 18 hours while monitoring by LCMS or HPLC for disappearance of the carboxylic acid and formation of the methyl ester. After completion, cool to room temperature and remove most of the methanol under reduced pressure. Dilute the residue with ethyl acetate and carefully wash with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate until acidic residues are neutralized, then wash with brine, dry the organic layer over anhydrous sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to afford the target methyl ester.

Cool to 0 °C and add thionyl chloride, O=S(Cl)Cl, 1.50 equiv, dropwise. Allow the mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 2.0 hours until gas evolution subsides. Remove solvent and excess thionyl chloride under reduced pressure, preferably with a dichloromethane or toluene co-evaporation, to give the crude acid chloride. Redissolve the residue in dry dichloromethane, 5 mL per mmol, and cool to 0 °C. Add a solution of CCC(F)(F)c1cccc(N)c1, 1.05 equiv, and triethylamine, CCN(CC)CC, 2.50 equiv, in dichloromethane dropwise. Stir at 0 °C for 15 minutes, then warm to 25 °C and stir for 3.0 hours. Monitor by LCMS or TLC for consumption of the acid chloride/intermediate. Quench carefully with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate, separate the organic layer, and extract the aqueous layer with dichloromethane. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography to obtain CCC(F)(F)c1cccc(NC(=O)c2c(C)nn(-c3ccc(OC)cc3)c2C(=O)OC)c1.

procedure: Dry the reaction vessel thoroughly and maintain a nitrogen or argon atmosphere. Charge the carboxylate-substituted aryl ethyl ketone substrate, 1.0 equiv, into the flask and dissolve or suspend it in anhydrous dichloromethane at approximately 0.05 M concentration.

The mixture was cooled on an ice-water bath to <5°C. and N,N-diisopropylethylamine (33.0 μL, 0.2 mmol) was added. Subsequently a solution of 2,6-difluorobenzoyl chloride (30 μL, 0.24 mmol) in acetonitrile (0.1 mL) was added dropwise keeping the temperature below 5°C. The temperature of the reaction mixture was allowed to come to room temperature. The mixture was partially diluted with ethyl acetate (5 mL) and water (3 mL) was added slowly. The resulting phases were separated and the water layer was extracted with ethyl acetate (3 mL). The combined organic layers were washed with water (5 mL), 5% NaHCO₃-solution (5 mL), water (5 mL) and brine (5 mL), filtered over a PE filter filled with Na₂SO₄ and concentrated under reduced pressure. The crude residue was purified by column chromatography (heptane to ethyl acetate=0 to 100 v/v %) to afford the title compound (72 mg, 72%) as a white solid.

patent_details: Methyl 3-oxobutanoate (2 mL, 18.5 mmol) was added dropwise to a solution of sodium methoxide (25% wt in MeOH, 5 mL) and anhydrous MeOH (20 mL). N-methyl thiourea (1.67 g, 18.5 mmol) was added to the reaction mixture. The resulting solution was stirred at reflux for 5 hours. After cooling to room temperature, the solvent was evaporated. The residue was dissolved in water (25 mL), and the solution was acidified to pH 2-3 with concentrated HCl. The solid material was recovered by filtration, washed with water (2×20 mL) and diethyl ether (1×30 mL), and dried in vacuo, affording 3,6-dimethyl-2-sulfanyl-3,4-dihydropyrimidin-4-one (2.16 g, 73% yield). The product was used without further purification.   A mixture of 2-(bromomethyl)-1,3,4-trichlorobenzene (576 mg, 2.1 mmol), 3,6-dimethyl-2-sulfanyl-3,4-dihydropyrimidin-4-one (300 mg, 1.9 mmol), and triethylamine (280 μL, 2.0 mmol) in absolute ethanol (10 mL) was stirred at room temperature overnight. The solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure. The solid product was suspended in water (30 mL). The solid material was recovered by filtration, washed with water (2×10 mL) and hexanes (2×20 mL), and dried in vacuo, affording the title compound (475 mg, 72% yield);¹H NMR (400 MHz, DMSO-d₆): δ 2.20 (s, 3H), 3.31 (s, 3H), 4.77 (s, 2H), 6.08 (s, 1H), 7.57 (d, 1H, J=8.8 Hz), 7.68 (d, 1H, J=8.8 Hz); M+ 350; HPLC purity: 95.8%.

patent_details: To an ice-cooled suspension of (3R)-1-benzyl-3-(3-methoxy-4-methylbenzyl)piperazine-2,5-dione (1.35 g) in tetrahydrofuran (22 ml) was added lithium aluminum hydride (0.378 g) at 5°C. or below under a nitrogen atmosphere. The mixture was stirred under reflux for 3 hours. After cooling the mixture to 5°C. or below, 2N sodium hydroxide was added to the mixture. After stirring the mixture for 30 minutes, insoluble matters were collected by filtration and washed with tetrahydrofuran. The filtrate and the washings were combined and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure to give (3R)-1-benzyl-3-(3-methoxy-4-methylbenzyl)piperazine in the form of an oily substance. A solution of 3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzoyl chloride (0.80 ml) in dichloromethane (1 ml) was added dropwise to an ice-cooled solution of (3R)-1-benzyl-3-(3-methoxy-4-methylbenzyl)-piperazine obtained by the above process and triethylamine (0.84 ml) in dichloromethane (10 ml) at 5°C. or below over 5 minutes. After stirring at the same temperature for 30 minutes, the reaction mixture was washed with an aqueous sodium chloride solution and dried over magnesium sulfate. The solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure. The residue was purified by silica gel column chromatography using a mixed solvent of hexane and ethyl acetate (4:1). Fractions containing the desired compound were collected and the solvent was evaporated under reduced pressure to give (2R)-4-benzyl-1-[3,5-bis(trifluoromethyl)benzoyl]-2-(3-methoxy-4-methylbenzyl)-piperazine (1.92 g) in the form of an oily substance. This is a highly matched transformation: the aldehyde forms an iminium ion with the secondary piperidine nitrogen, followed by selective reduction to give the N-cyclopropylmethyl tertiary amine. The retrieved examples are close analogues using secondary piperidines plus cyclic aldehydes in chlorinated solvent with NaBH(OAc)3 at room temperature overnight.

If solubility in dichloromethane is poor, replace dichloromethane with 1,2-dichloroethane, matching the retrieved precedent more closely. Reaction temperature and reagent loading can remain the same. This is a minor solvent optimization rather than a change in route.

Adding a small amount of acetic acid could accelerate iminium formation, but it is not necessary based on the retrieved precedents and may increase side reactions or salt formation. Therefore it is not the first recommendation.

Cool the solution to 0 °C and add cyclopropanecarboxaldehyde, O=CC1CC1, 1.2 equivalents. Add sodium triacetoxyborohydride, 1.5 equivalents, portionwise at 0 °C. Stir at 0 °C for 15 minutes, then allow the mixture to warm to 22 °C and stir for 16 hours. Monitor conversion by LC-MS or TLC. After completion, quench carefully with 1 N aqueous NaOH or saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate to pH about 8-9. Separate the layers and extract the aqueous phase with dichloromethane or ethyl acetate. Combine the organic layers, wash with water and brine, dry over anhydrous sodium sulfate or magnesium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography, for example dichloromethane/methanol with a small amount of ammonia or triethylamine if tailing occurs, to afford O=C1CCc2cc(OC3CCN(CC4CC4)CC3)ccc2N1c1ccc(F)cc1.

Add triethylamine, 4.0 equiv, followed by catalytic DMAP, 0.10 equiv. Cool the mixture to 0 °C. Prepare a separate solution of cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride, 2.5 equiv, in about 5 mL dry dichloromethane, and add it dropwise over approximately 30 min while maintaining 0 °C. After addition, allow the reaction mixture to warm to 25 °C and stir for 16 h. Monitor by LC-MS or TLC for disappearance of starting diol/phenol and monoacylated intermediates. If monoacylated material remains, add an additional 0.3 equiv cyclohexanecarbonyl chloride and 0.5 equiv triethylamine and stir for 2-4 h. Quench carefully at 0 °C with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate. Separate the organic layer and wash successively with water, dilute aqueous citric acid or dilute HCl to remove amines, saturated sodium bicarbonate, and brine. Dry the organic phase over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate under reduced pressure. Purify the residue by silica gel chromatography, for example using hexane/ethyl acetate or dichloromethane/methanol gradients, to afford the desired bis-cyclohexanecarboxylate product.

patent_details: 1-Fluoro-2-methyl-4-nitrobenzene (1.32 g, 8.49 mmol) was added to a suspension of 6-chloropyridin-3-ol (1 g, 7.72 mmol) and potassium carbonate (2.13 g, 15.44 mmol) in N,N-dimethylformamide (20 mL). The reactants were reacted at 70°C. for 16 hours, then cooled to room temperature, poured into water (100 mL), and extracted with ethyl acetate (50 mL×3). The organic phases were combined, washed with saturated brine (100 mL), dried over anhydrous sodium sulfate, filtered, and concentrated. The residue obtained was isolated and purified by silica gel column to give 1.86 g of yellow oil in 91% yield.

full_recipe.procedure: On a 1.00 mmol scale, charge a dry flask with the preserved reactant mixture corresponding to 2-fluoro-5-nitrotoluene, Oc1ccc(Cl)nc1, and cesium carbonate: use 1.00 equiv aryl fluoride, 1.05 equiv chlorohydroxypyridine, and 2.00 equiv Cs2CO3. Add dry DMF at 5.0 mL per mmol of aryl fluoride. Stir under nitrogen at 80 °C for 16 h and monitor by LC-MS or TLC for disappearance of the aryl fluoride. Cool to room temperature, dilute with water, and extract with ethyl acetate. Wash the combined organic layers with water and brine, dry over Na2SO4 or MgSO4, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude residue by silica gel chromatography, for example hexane/ethyl acetate gradient, to afford Cc1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1Oc1ccc(Cl)nc1.

reagents.name: sodium hydride, preferably 60% dispersion in mineral oil
reagents.amount: 2.50 mmol NaH; 100 mg of 60% dispersion per 1.00 mmol substrate

full_recipe.procedure: Under nitrogen or argon, suspend sodium hydride, 60% dispersion in mineral oil, 2.5 equiv, in dry DMF at 0 °C. Add a solution of COC(=O)Cc1nc2c(C#N)c(C)c(-c3ccccc3)c(Cl)n2n1, 1.0 equiv, in dry DMF slowly, maintaining 0 °C. Stir for 30 minutes at 0 °C to form the enolate. Add methyl iodide, 3.0 equiv, dropwise at 0 °C. Allow the reaction to warm to 25 °C and stir for about 6 hours, monitoring by LCMS or HPLC. If mono-methylated intermediate remains, add an additional 0.5 equiv NaH and 0.5 equiv MeI and continue stirring. When complete, cool to 0 °C and carefully quench dropwise with saturated aqueous ammonium chloride. Dilute with ethyl acetate, separate the layers, wash the organic phase with water and brine, dry over sodium sulfate, filter, and concentrate. Purify the crude product by silica gel chromatography or preparative HPLC to obtain COC(=O)C(C)(C)c1nc2c(C#N)c(C)c(-c3ccccc3)c(Cl)n2n1.
